detail:
The National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI) reports that it leads and supports research on sleep health and sleep disorders, including sleep apnea, through its Division of Lung Diseases and the National Center on Sleep Disorders Research. NHLBI-supported research is credited in the sources with helping define the links between sleep apnea and other serious health conditions, including obesity, type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, stroke, and heart disease.

Landmark work described by NHLBI includes the Apnea Positive Pressure Long-term Efficacy Study (APPLES), which found continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy to be an effective treatment, a partnership study finding that sleep apnea affects more than 80 percent of people who have both obesity and type 2 diabetes, and the Childhood Adenotonsillectomy Trial (CHAT) on tonsil surgery in children. Current research described in the sources covers new treatments such as pharmacotherapy and innovative devices, healthy lifestyle approaches, and how sleep apnea affects women, including during pregnancy.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about sleep apnea research and clinical trials.
sourceName: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute
summary: NHLBI describes its sleep apnea research as establishing links to obesity, diabetes, blood pressure, stroke, and heart disease, and as supporting current work on new medicines, devices, lifestyle approaches, and sleep apnea in women and children.
takeaways: research links sleep apnea to heart and metabolic conditions
landmark trials studied cpap, diabetes overlap, and child surgery
new medicines and devices remain investigational in the sources
title: Sleep apnea: research on heart, metabolic, and treatment links
